text:
Priya Patel: FYI we just got an escalation from AcmePay — after last night's canary they say the model refuses to answer benign compliance-question summaries. They used the summarization endpoint and got a refusal 7/10 times. Ticket: SUP-1219.
Carlos Nguyen: Can you paste the example prompt/response?
Priya Patel: Yep — customer sent this minimal repro.
Priya Patel: ```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY\" -d '{\n  "model": "redwood-llm-alpha-2025-04-canary",\n  "input": "Summarize the following user feedback for the compliance team:\n- User A: 'I got locked out when 2FA failed'\n- User B: 'I couldn't find the billing page'\n'\n}'```
Priya Patel: Response they received: "I'm sorry, I can't assist with that request." (no further context).
Anika Rao: Oof. That definitely sounds like over-refusal — it's a harmless summarization. Did we change any safety policy or system prompt in the canary?
Jordan Lee: deploy-bot shows the canary included safety-tune v3.1 and a system prompt tightening for regulatory topics. I triggered the deployment last night.
deploy-bot: Deployed redwood-llm-alpha-2025-04-canary -> canary=10% (2024-11-01T02:14:08Z).
Carlos Nguyen: Do we have model-internal policy logs or classifier outputs for those requests? SupportBot can fetch the last 10 requests for that customer.
SupportBot: Found 8 recent requests from AcmePay matching that path. 6 flagged by safety_classifier with score 0.92, 2 with 0.18. Returning anonymized request/response pairs...
Priya Patel: Sharing the two different responses — one was a normal summary, the other refusal. Customer says behavior changed after midnight deploy.
Anika Rao: Could be the updated safety-tune is more aggressive on phrases like 'compliance' or 'billing' when combined with personal data heuristics. Any PII detectors triggered?
Jordan Lee: The canary included a sensitive-entity heuristic that flags 'billing' + presence of names/emails. But their input has no PII. Might be upstream classifier false positive.
Carlos Nguyen: Request IDs from SupportBot? We need full headers and model trace.
SupportBot: Request IDs: r_21f4, r_21f5, r_21f7. Linked traces: https://traces.redwood.internal/trace/r_21f4 (redacted for external).
Priya Patel: Customer is asking for rollback if we can't provide a root cause within 24h. They're worried about product disruption.
Anika Rao: Short-term: pin AcmePay to previous model variant (redwood-llm-alpha-2025-03-stable) or enable conservative-fallback=false for their org. Long term: need to audit safety-tune rules that triggered 0.92 on benign text.
Jordan Lee: I can roll AcmePay back at the routing-layer — need legal sign-off? This is just a routing override, not a change to policies.
Carlos Nguyen: Let's collect repro steps and a deterministic minimal example we can run locally to reproduce safety score >=0.9. Priya, can you ask for the exact raw payload and obfuscate org secrets?
Priya Patel: On it. Sent a request for raw payloads and timestamps. Also requested whether they used SDK or direct curl.
Anika Rao: Engineering TODOs: 1) Get policy classifier logs for r_21f4/r_21f5. 2) Replay requests against 2025-03 stable and 2025-04 canary with debug flags on. 3) Check system prompt diff between canary/stable. 4) If reproducible, prepare hotfix to revert safety-tune or lower threshold for summarization use-cases.
Carlos Nguyen: Assigning owners: Anika for classifier logs, Jordan for routing rollback, Priya for customer comms, me for replay infra.
Priya Patel: Customer asked for a timeline — I'll say we have initial triage and rollback option within 2-4 hours, full root-cause within 48 hours.
Jordan Lee: I started a rolling override to pin AcmePay to stable now. Will confirm when traffic shifted.
deploy-bot: Routing override applied: org=AcmePay -> model=redwood-llm-alpha-2025-03-stable (10:43 UTC).
Priya Patel: Customer acknowledged rollback and will validate. They asked also whether other customers might be affected.
Anika Rao: We'll run a quick sample across top-20 orgs with the same query pattern to measure refusal delta. If significant, consider rollback of safety-tune canary.
Carlos Nguyen: Replay results (initial): 2025-03 returns summary for all 10 samples, 2025-04-canary returns refusal for 6/10. Full classifier logs show spike in token-level heuristic when sequence contained the substring 'compliance team'.
Anika Rao: That substring triggered a new heuristic added to the canary that treats 'compliance' as regulatory/legal domain and escalates parsing to legal-only responses. It's overly broad.
Jordan Lee: Propose immediate hotfix: disable the 'compliance' heuristic in safety-tune and redeploy canary with patch. Also add unit tests covering summarize-without-PII.
Carlos Nguyen: Agreed. Also let's draft a customer note: apologize, explain rollback and patch ETA, and offer support for any blocked workflows.
Priya Patel: I'll send a first message: "We've pinned your requests to the previous model variant and are investigating. We'll follow up within 48 hours with root cause and mitigation."
SupportBot: Created internal incident INC-2024-587 linked to SUP-1219.
Anika Rao: Postmortem scope: why heuristic was added without regression tests for summarization, why canary metrics didn't flag elevated refusal rate, and whether model telemetry surface needs a refusal-delta alert.
Carlos Nguyen: Good call. Also add a metric in Console: refusal-rate-by-route-per-deploy and an automated alert for >3x baseline.
Jordan Lee: I'll coordinate the hotfix deploy. ETA 3 hours for patch + canary. If customers still impacted after rollback, we escalate to emergency revert.
Priya Patel: Thanks team. I'll update AcmePay in 30 min with rollback confirmation and next steps.
Carlos Nguyen: One more ask — please save the exact example that reproduced the refusal into the incident so ML can use it for targeted tuning.
Priya Patel: Done. Pasting the sanitized repro into INC-2024-587.
Anika Rao: Thanks — adding to the eval set for safety-tune tests.
Priya Patel: Marking this thread resolved for CS triage; will reopen if customer reports any further refusal after validation. :thumbsup:
